questions.title: SOLID Overview
questions.question: What does SOLID stand for? Give a one-line description of each principle.
questions.realWorldScenario: Every Java/Spring Boot interview — SOLID is a universal litmus test for code quality awareness.

questions.title: Single Responsibility Principle
questions.question: What is the Single Responsibility Principle? Give an example of a violation and how to fix it.
questions.realWorldScenario: A UserService that handles user CRUD, sends emails, and generates PDFs — three responsibilities.

questions.title: Open/Closed Principle
questions.question: What is the Open/Closed Principle? How does it relate to adding new features without modifying existing code?
questions.realWorldScenario: Adding a new payment method without touching the existing checkout logic.

questions.title: Liskov Substitution Principle
questions.question: What is the Liskov Substitution Principle? Give an example of a violation.
questions.realWorldScenario: Square extends Rectangle but violates LSP because setting width changes height.

questions.title: Interface Segregation Principle
questions.question: What is the Interface Segregation Principle? How do you apply it when designing interfaces in Java?
questions.realWorldScenario: A Worker interface with work() and eat() forces Robot to implement eat() — split into Workable and Eatable.

questions.title: Dependency Inversion Principle
questions.question: What is the Dependency Inversion Principle? How does Spring's dependency injection implement it?
questions.realWorldScenario: Injecting a UserRepository interface rather than the concrete JpaUserRepository — Spring handles the binding.

questions.title: SOLID in Spring Boot
questions.question: Can you identify where Spring Boot applies SOLID principles in its own design?
questions.realWorldScenario: Demonstrating depth of knowledge in a senior-track fresher interview.
